text:
alex_w: Heads-up: planning to bump aws provider + gpufleet module to v3 in the gitops repo. This includes an AMI family switch and a small shape change on the KMS alias input. Want to run this canary-safe — we have reserved pools in us-west-2 that are sensitive to AMI changes.

maria_ops: Thanks Alex. Can you paste the diff you plan to merge?

alex_w: Sure — high level: gpufleet module v2 -> v3. Provider upgrade from 4.x -> 5.x. tf changes: 
```hcl
module "gpufleet" {
  source = "github.com/redwood/gpufleet//modules/pool?ref=v3"
  ami_family = "ubuntu-24-ami" -> "ubuntu-24-optimized"
  kms_alias = var.kms_alias (was string) -> { name = var.kms_alias_name }
}
```
The provider bump also changes default behavior for CreateBeforeDestroy on autoscaling groups (we'll lose some blue/green semantics).

kevin_sre: Oof. AMI family swaps always risk host driver/kernel mismatches with GPU kernel modules. We should gate us-west-2 clusters behind a canary az and restrict spot fallback.

maria_ops: Also noticed the KMS alias shape change will fail the gitops CI lint (schema mismatch) unless we add a compat shim in the module to accept string and map.

infra-bot: terraform plan failed in preview pipeline: error: Incompatible value for variable "kms_alias": string required.

sam_platform: For safety I suggest a two-stage rollout: 1) module accepts both shapes (compat shim) + no-op migration; 2) Canaries in single AZ (us-west-2a) with reduced capacity; 3) Monitor kernel crashloop rates + pod eviction. If green, progressively increase.

priya_sec: KMS change also touches IAM: the new shape will cause the module to create a new kms:Alias resource if not careful. We need explicit alias policy + a migration doc so audit logs don't show unexpected key creations. Also add a test that keys are not recreated in staging.

alex_w: Agreed on shim. I'll open a small PR that:
- accepts kms_alias as string or object
- maps old string form to { name = string } internally
- pins provider to 4.x in the canary branch (so we can test gpufleet v3 without immediate provider upgrade)

maria_ops: Good — pinning provider in canary branch reduces blast radius. How will we run the canary? Manual apply or gitops with a patch?

sam_platform: Use a dedicated gitops overlay branch `canary/gpufleet-ami-kms` that the GitOps pipeline watches. The pipeline should:
- create a canary workspace in the org TF state (separate state file)
- set `reserved_capacity_override = 10%` and `allow_spot_fallback = false`
- annotate pool with `redwood:canary=true` label for routing

kevin_sre: Monitoring: add temporary eBPF probe to collect GPU driver OOPS and a pod eviction alert rule (5m spike > 3%). Also track node GPU utilization and NVSwitch errors.

maria_ops: CI checks we need before merge: 
- `terraform validate` + schema tests (accept old/new kms shape)
- a plan diff that shows no resource destroy for existing KMS keys
- an automated canary smoke apply job that runs the canary overlay against test account in us-west-2

infra-bot: gitops pipeline: canary overlay deploy started by `gh pr comment /deploy-canary`. Current status: queued.

alex_w: Pushing PR with shim + docs in 10m. Will include rollback steps: revert overlay branch, set provider pin back, run `terraform apply` to revert pool config, and a manual AMI rollback image list.

priya_sec: Add a checkpoint for security review of the alias migration script. If there's an alias rename we must rotate access grants via IAM roles.

sam_platform: Cost note: running canary with reserved instances still counts toward committed capacity. We should ensure finance is aware — set `cost_center=canary-gpufleet` tag so chargeback works.

maria_ops: One more thing: networking — changing AMI may bump kernel sysctl defaults. We need to watch host-level MTU errors in CNI logs during canary. Add a quick grep in the canary smoke test: `journalctl -k | grep -i mtu || true`.

kevin_sre: If anything spikes, operator policy: immediate revert, scale down canary pool to zero, and failover workloads to regional fallback in us-east-1. Make runbook step 3 clear.

alex_w: PR: https://github.com/redwood/gpufleet/pull/867 (draft) — includes shim + provider pin in canary branch + docs. Requesting reviewers: @maria_ops @kevin_sre @priya_sec @sam_platform.

maria_ops: Reviewing now. If CI is green for schema tests and smoke apply succeeds in the test account, we can schedule the canary during low-traffic window Fri 02:00 UTC.

infra-bot: canary smoke apply succeeded in test account (us-west-2 test): plan shows no KMS create, one instance replacement queued in canary pool (rolling update), no IAM changes.

kevin_sre: Nice. Proceed with monitoring hooks. I'll stand by for the 02:00 UTC window.

priya_sec: Approved the migration doc with one note about audit log retention.

alex_w: Thanks all. Will merge draft -> canary branch and kick the overlay deploy. I'll post a short update to #incidents if we see any failures. :thumbsup:

maria_ops: Good job — clear rollback plan. Keep notes in the runbook under /runbooks/gpufleet/ami-kms-migration.md

sam_platform: Tagging finance: `@finance` pls watch for `cost_center=canary-gpufleet` charges next week.

infra-bot: canary overlay deployed to canary/gpufleet-ami-kms at 2398765724."
